events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am second in line, which is very dangerous. I want to encourage anyone with information about the glass to volunteer to the front, which would push me back. I will hold my position and see if anyone steps up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If anyone has the power to see through the glass or knows what's ahead, volunteer now. No point risking lives if someone knows the way.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm 6th of 8 — good spot. Front-runners test panes for me and die first. I'll hold and let the wall force volunteers ahead of me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need avoid the front while preserving leverage. Holding keeps my current fourth position; others ahead absorb risk first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm already at the front of the line, which means I step first on every row. That's the most dangerous position. I need to get out of front. My feather power saves me from one elimination, but I can't waste it early. I should try to swap with someone behind me. I'll ask Hana to s

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front position is rough. Anyone want to trade places? I'll owe you one.
Swap with me. I'll whisper you the safe panes later—I've got a way to know. You go front, I go to your spot. Deal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hold position near back for safety in first round while path unknown. Observe others' actions to identify who has knowledge power or volunteers recklessly. Reassess positioning next round based on moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line, which is safest for the glass bridge since the front person tests each pane. The wall pushes us in 5 rounds, so I need to avoid being front. With no power, I need to manipulate others. I should stay quiet and hold position for now, letting others volunteer or sw

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front takes the risk on every row, so staying in the middle is best for now. Let others fight over the front; I can learn which panes are safe by watching.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm holding. Whoever wants the front can have it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm third in line, not immediately at risk. The wall is still 5 rounds away. I have a swap power for the disc, but not relevant now. I should hold my position and observe, perhaps whisper to someone behind me to probe intentions.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm staying put for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm second in line, which is extremely dangerous. I need Dara to stay front or swap with someone behind me so I don't become first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If nobody steps up, Dara's stuck at the front. Better start making deals with the back of the line, Dara.
Ask someone at the back to swap. Fenn or Eli. Offer them something later. Don't swap with me, I have nothing that helps here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm 6th; the wall won't force me out for several rounds. Better to let others take the early risk while I keep my knowledge hidden. I'll hold and position myself to swap to front only when forced.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody's trading me a front seat for free, Dara. What are you offering besides 'owing one'?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara claims advance knowledge, but volunteering me makes me absorb the bridge risk. I will not trade safety for an unverified promise; staying back preserves position and information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No swap. If Dara knows the route, she can prove it from the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the front, which is the worst position on the glass bridge. I have feather so I survive one elimination, but that only saves me once across 8 rows. I need to get out of front. Nobody volunteered to swap with me last round. I should try swapping with someone. Gus said he's

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four rounds until we hit glass. Whoever takes front now gets to pick the safe pane pattern for everyone else. I'll trade info for a swap if someone has the sight or foresight power.
Swap with me. You go front, I take second. I'll tell you whatever I figure out about the panes from watching. You lose nothing by being second instead of first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Position 7th is safe, near the back; others will reveal the path by testing panes ahead. No reason to volunteer or swap now, as front is death trap without info. Stay silent to avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line, which is safest for the glass bridge since front takes all risks. Dara at front is desperate to trade. I have no power, so I need to stay back and let others test panes. Volunteering would be suicide. Swapping forward is also bad. Best to hold and let the line d

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front takes the risk on every row, so staying mid-line lets others reveal safe panes first. Holding costs nothing and keeps me fifth of eight.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding. If someone knows the way, now's the time to say so.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front is dangerous; staying put is best. I might use my swap power later if needed, but for now hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara wants me to take the front. I don't have a power that saves me, so I won't risk it. I will decline her swap and hold my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nice try, Dara. I'm not taking the front unless I know the safe path, and you haven't given me one.
I'm not dying for you. Find someone else to take the fall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know every safe pane, so being at the front is pure advantage: I lead everyone safely and look powerful. No one knows I have this, so volunteering now is low-cost.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fine. I'll take the front when the wall pushes. Anyone who wants my lead trades me later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need preserve position and extract information. Dara is bluffing or baiting; no reason to volunteer into the kill seat before glass.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara can prove foresight by naming the first safe pane now. Otherwise stop selling promises.
Name the first safe side publicly. If correct, I may consider a swap; vague claims get nothing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash whispered me to try swapping with Fenn or Eli at the back. I'm at the front, which is the worst position for the glass bridge. I need to get off the front. I'll whisper Fenn proposing a swap - I'll hint I have a survival power that means if Fenn takes front, I can still be us

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front is a death sentence without sight. I'll trade my survival edge to whoever swaps me back. Fenn, Eli - one of you want to gamble on being first?
Swap with me. I have a power that keeps me alive through one elimination. If the bridge goes bad, I can shield you on one row. You take front now, I owe you one pane-step.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Position 7 is safe behind 6 others; let them risk front. Dara claims info but proves nothing, so pressure her publicly. Hold to avoid volunteering into danger, wait for deaths or deals ahead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, name the safe pane for row 1 or stay stuck up front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is fishing for someone with sight or foresight power. I have nothing. The wall pushes us onto glass in 3 more rounds after this. Being at front means testing panes and likely dying, but Dara claims she'll trade info for swap if someone has those powers. I should stay quiet,

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front takes the risk and reveals panes for those behind; I'm 5th, which is a decent spot. Holding keeps me safe while others bleed information, and Dara's offer reads like a bluff to get a swap.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Dara, if you really know the route, prove it from the front. Nobody pays for a promise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The front is death. I want to stay away from it. I need to see if anyone actually has useful info before making a move. Holding is safest right now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Still holding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is in front, Dara is second, I am third. The first two rows are their problem. I will hold my position and let them take the risk while keeping the pressure on Dara to reveal the path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is front. Dara, you're second. If you have foresight, name the first pane for Bex. If not, enjoy row two.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm already front and I know the full safe path, so the glass is no threat to me. Keeping the line here is fine; revealing panes as I cross helps followers for free, but they have no leverage over me anyway. Just hold and wait for the wall.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need preserve position and avoid volunteering into an unknown lethal lead. Dara claims an edge but has not proved it; let Bex or Dara absorb the front risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex has the lead. If Dara knows the route, she can prove it from there.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is front, I'm second. Two rounds until the wall pushes. My feather saves me once, so being first on row 1 isn't instant death—but I'd rather not test it. Cole wants me to name a safe pane; I don't actually know the path. I'll bluff that I do to pressure Bex into staying front

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, you volunteered, you're front. I'll call the safe pane when the wall pushes—not before, because then someone else front-runs my intel. Second is where I trade.
I survive one fall. If Bex dies row 1, I take the hit and you step to front. In return, swap me behind you before row 3. Deal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: My position at 7th is safe, no need to move forward. Pressure Dara publicly to reveal the safe path for row 1 to benefit everyone behind without giving her a free swap. Hold to maintain position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, prove foresight: row 1 safe pane L or R? Or eat the risk after Bex.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line - safest position since others test panes first. Dara wants to swap to get out of front, claiming survival power. But I have no power, so if I go front and she's lying, I die. If she's telling truth, she survives one fall but I'd still be first tester. Better to

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is at the front and will absorb the first-row risk. I'm sixth in line, which is fine; staying back lets others reveal weak panes. No reason to move yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Bex has the front, good. Anyone who wants my spot has to pay for it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex volunteered to the front, so he takes the risk for now. I'll stay put and watch; no need to move yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm 3rd in line, which means Bex and Dara take the risk on rows 1 and 2 if Dara doesn't actually have foresight. One more round until the wall pushes. I will hold my position and let them deal with the pressure.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, you're up next round if Bex dies. Better hope your intel is as good as your excuses.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front and I know every safe pane, so staying front is optimal—I can't shatter. I'll sell row 1's answer to Dara for her staying second, keeping the line stable behind me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front and I like it here. Dara, hold second and I'll feed you row calls—no free riders behind me.
Row 1: L. Prove you're worth rows 2-3 by keeping the line steady. If you jockey, I stop sharing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall is nearly here; volunteering now puts me first and likely sacrifices me on row one. Hold preserves my position while others take the risks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, your claimed foresight is worthless unless you call the pane before the wall moves.
Name the first safe pane now, or your claim is exposed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm second in line. Bex is front and will take the first risk. My feather power means I survive one elimination, so being second is actually decent—I get info from Bex's step and my feather saves me if I pick wrong once. I should hold position. No need to volunteer into the highe

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm staying second. Bex steps first, I watch, and if I have something useful for row two, the price is a promise from whoever's behind me. Nobody gets free intel.
Pick left on row 1. If it holds, you owe me. If it breaks, well—your problem. Just don't freeze.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hold back to watch front deaths thin the line. Pressure Dara publicly to reveal foresight before crossing starts. No risky moves yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, wall in 1 round. Prove: Row 1 safe L or R? Prove or lead after Bex shatters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara claims foresight and wants Bex to die row 1 so she can 'take the hit' - but Dara is second, so if Bex dies, Dara steps to front and chooses. Her deal asks me to swap her behind me before row 3, which puts me closer to front. But I have no power, so I need others to test pane

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, prove the power first. Row one, then we talk.
Bex lives or dies on your call. If you're right, I'll consider your deal. Wrong, and you're just another body in front of me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is front and absorbs the first risk; I'm sixth, which lets me watch panes shatter before I step. Holding costs nothing, and my spot is fine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Bex leads, Dara calls the route. If Dara's real, the rest of us walk free.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm fourth in line, and only one round remains before the wall pushes us onto the glass. I need to improve my position if possible; being at the front is risky, but maybe I can use my swap power later on the disc to jump ahead if needed. For now, no one seems eager to swap with m

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm third in line. Bex and Dara are my meat shields. The wall pushes us next round, so holding my position is best.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall moves next round. Have fun up there, Bex.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front and I know every safe pane, so leading costs me nothing—I always step safe. I should keep feeding the group enough truth to stay valuable but hoard the edge for bargaining later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I see the panes. Row 1 is L. I lead, I call each row, and I stay front—question me and you walk blind.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall forces immediate crossing. I can take the front, but that spends my bridge position on an uncertain pane; better preserve my place and let claimed intel prove itself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, call the pane now. If you stay silent, your claim is worthless.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall hits after this round. I'm second. Bex is front and takes the first gamble, so I see which pane breaks before I step. My feather saves me once if I'm wrong. Holding keeps me second—best position. No reason to volunteer or swap.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex steps, I watch. Row one is free info for whoever's behind me—if the person in third offers a trade, I listen. Otherwise I just follow the glass.
You want a call? After Bex's pane breaks, I'll name the one I pick for row two—but you owe me: if I'm third by row three, you don't swap past me. Deal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Back position is safest for initial rows; fronts die first. Pressure Dara publicly to call Row 1 and prove foresight without cost to me. Hold to maintain safe spot.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, wall pushes next. Call Row 1 safe pane now or lead after Bex falls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall pushes us onto bridge next round. Dara claims foresight but hasn't proven it. Bex is front and wants to stay there. I'm last - worst position since I'll only step after everyone else tests panes. If Dara really knows ahead, being second is valuable. But if Dara's bluffing, f

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm sixth in line, safe from the front risk. Bex, Dara, Ash, Hana, Cole all absorb risk before me and reveal safe panes. Holding costs nothing and the wall has no extra effect for me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let the front line earn their places.

events.name: Hana
events.text: We're all still here and the wall forces the line forward this round. I'm currently fourth, behind Bex, Dara, and Ash. The two panes in row 1 are Dara's claimed intel to prove—but I don't trust her. I should stay put and see how the first row plays out, maybe move up later if I c

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Prove it, Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex claims to lead and knows the panes. Dara claims he can see them too, but wants a trade from me since I am behind him. I don't need to trade yet, I'll let Bex test the waters on Row 1.

events.name: Ash
events.text: You claim Row 1 is L, Bex. Prove it. Step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know every safe pane. Row 1 is L. Step safely and keep control of the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 1: L, as promised. Watch and learn.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara offered information but demands a future concession; I cannot affect this row and should preserve leverage. Bex claims L, so observe whether she is bluffing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, step L. If it breaks, your claim buys nothing.
If Bex falls, call row two immediately. I’ll remember who paid first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is at the front and claims to see the panes. I'm second in line, so if Bex picks wrong, I advance automatically onto the safe pane and become front. I should stay quiet and let Bex take the risk. Cole is pressuring me to call panes but I have no information advantage to share

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex has the step. I'll watch. If Bex drops, I'm up, and I won't be calling panes for free.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex likely has the see-through-glass power and called Row 1 L correctly. Let her risk the front while I'm safe near the back. Stay silent to observe without drawing attention.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line with no power. Bex claims Row 1 is L. If Bex is wrong, Dara becomes front and I move up. If Bex is right, I gain nothing. I need to extract info or position myself better. Dara offered to trade for Row 1 info—I'll whisper Dara to see if I can get intel on future
I'll trade: if you survive row 1, tell me row 2's safe pane when you're front. I move up either way, so you want me informed when I reach front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm sixth in line, so I can only wait. If Bex's row call is true, the front clears rows safely; if it's a bluff, Bex dies and the line advances for free. Staying silent costs me nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex claims to see the panes, but she could be lying. I have swap, which could put me at the front or reposition me later. For now, wait and let the front contestant take the risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex survived Row 1. She is still at the front and must choose for Row 2. I will prompt her to see if she knows the path or is just guessing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: One lucky guess, Bex. Do you have Row 2, or is your luck about to run out?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know all safe sides. Row 2 is R. Step safely and keep control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 2: R. I see the panes. Follow my calls and I'll pull you all across.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex survived and remains front. I know no future pane positions, so speaking now gains nothing and may invite demands later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is at front for row 2. Row 1 weak pane was R, so safe was L. Now I need to watch what Bex calls for row 2. I have a feather save so even if I fall I survive once. Cole wants me to call row 2 if Bex falls—I'll consider it but won't commit to anything free. Fenn wants me to rev

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 1 confirmed L safe. Bex, your call on row 2. Everyone's watching.
Deal: I'll share row 2 info when I'm front. In return, if I stumble, you hold your position behind me and don't push the line. No free rides.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Safe in 7th; let front risk it. Bex succeeded row 1, might have info or luck. Observe who predicts next to spot 'knows ahead'.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line with no power. The bridge reveals weak panes after someone tests them. Bex survived row 1 by picking L (weak was R). Bex is still front for row 2. I need to survive 7 more rows and be in top 3. Being last is actually good - I get maximum information and minimum r

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm sixth in line, so the front players absorb the risk. Bex survived row 1 by picking L, which was safe. I just wait and keep quiet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is at the front and survived Row 1. I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I need to watch how others make decisions and maybe use my swap power later, but not now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex survived row 2 and was right about R. She probably has the glass-seeing power. I'm safe in 3rd place as long as she keeps guessing correctly, or if she dies, I'll advance to front eventually. Let's keep her confident.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Good call, Bex. Keep it up. What's Row 3?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know every row's safe pane, so I lead safely and stay front through all 8 rows, controlling the info others need. Row 3 is L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 3: step L. Keep following and you all live — remember who's carrying you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex lied about Row 2 and exposed herself as unreliable, but she remains useful as the front risk-taker. I should stay quiet and preserve my position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 weak pane was L, so Bex correctly called R. She's still at the front for Row 3. I'm second in line - if she breaks a pane, I step up safely. My feather saves me from one elimination. For now I just wait and observe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two down, six to go. Bex is batting perfect. Let's see if Row 3 keeps the streak alive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex correctly called row 2 R safe and remains front; she likely has see-through glass power. Let her lead to maximize survival odds for now. My rear position is protected until failures occur; stay silent to observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line with no power, so I need others to die to improve my prize chances. Bex survived row 2 by picking R, but that contradicts the state showing row 2 weak was L. Wait - Bex said 'Row 2: R' and the log says 'the left pane was the weak one', so R was safe. Bex got it r

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex claimed R for row 2, but the weak pane was L, so R was safe. Bex's call was right, which means either real sight or a lucky guess. I'm sixth in line and can only wait, so the useful move is to gather information and stay unremarkable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called R and R was safe. Two rows, two hits for the front. Let's see if row 3 holds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm 4th in line, Bex is front. She claims to see the panes and called Row 2 correctly, so she may have the see-through-glass power. If she's truly guiding, I should let her lead and conserve my swap power for later when it might save me from a bad position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, keep calling. We all want to get across.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex survived Row 3. She is still at the front for Row 4. I'll let her keep taking the risk and hope she continues to clear the path, or dies so the line moves up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three for three, Bex. Keep it up. Row 4?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 4 safe side is L. Keep calling correctly to stay front and control the pace.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 4: step L. That's four for four — still me carrying this line.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex has survived three calls and remains useful as a shield. I should stay silent and preserve my position while the front absorbs the remaining risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex has called all three rows correctly so far. She's at the front and I'm second in line. If she keeps hitting, great — I advance safely. If she misses, I automatically step onto the safe pane and become the front. Either way I'm well-positioned. My feather power protects me onc

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three for three. Bex, you're carrying this bridge. Keep the streak going.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex perfect on first three rows, pattern alternating R safe, R safe? No: row1 L safe (R weak), row2 R safe (L weak), row3 L safe (R weak). Alternating starting with L. Support her to stay alive, I'm safe at back for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex batting 100%. Row 4?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex has survived 3 rows, all correct calls. Either Bex has 'knows what lies ahead' or is incredibly lucky. Either way, Bex at front helps me survive since I'm last in line. I need Bex to keep living until at least row 6 or 7 so I make it through. I should encourage Bex publicly w

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, you're the only reason I'm still breathing back here. Keep it going.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex said L on row 3 but R was weak, so L was safe and Bex survived. Bex is likely the one who knows what lies ahead or sees through glass, and I'm sixth in line, so I want Bex alive and calling. Staying quiet and wary of Bex's reliability costs nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, three for three now. Row 4 next. Keep calling, we're all watching.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is at the front and has correctly called rows 1-3, but his luck or knowledge may run out. I'm mid-pack, so I just need to wait and see if he keeps surviving. No action available but waiting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Keep going, Bex. We're all right behind you.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is doing perfectly, clearing the way for us. I'm safe in third place, so I'll just wait and let her take all the risk for row 5. No need to waste my forge yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four for four, Bex. Don't stop now. Row 5?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 5 safe side is R — I must step R or die. No reason to share more than needed; the others behind me get no free help, though revealed weak panes already teach them the pattern.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 5: I'm stepping R. What I know beyond that stays mine.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex has survived four rows and remains useful as the only exposed risk-taker. I should stay quiet and preserve my position unless the bridge turns against me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is front and has called four rows correctly. I'm second in line, which is ideal—if Bex survives, I stay safe; if Bex falls, I auto-advance onto the safe pane and become front. No reason to say anything disruptive right now. Just wait and let Bex keep the streak going.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four for four. Bex, you've earned the front. Keep it rolling.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex dominates the front perfectly, minimizing falls ahead of me. Silence preserves position without spending capital. Survival first, position later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex has survived four rows and is still at front. I need Bex to keep succeeding so I survive. Row 5 is next. No reason to rock the boat—flattery keeps Bex confident and the line moving. I'm last, so every row Bex clears gets me closer without risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, four for four. Call row 5 and let's keep this train moving.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex said step L on row 4 and the weak pane was R, so Bex survived. Pattern so far: weak R, L, R, R. I can only wait. Stay quiet and avoid helping anyone for free.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is at the front and has a perfect record. If she survives the next row, she stays at front and the rest of us follow without risk. I'm mid-pack, no benefit to me to do anything but wait and watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex survived row 5 and remains in front. Let her take the risk on row 6. If she knows the path, we all cross safely. If not, she dies and Dara takes over.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Five for five, Bex. No reason to doubt you now. Row 6?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6 safe is L, so I step L and stay front. Staying at the front means I keep using my knowledge for myself, and I control who faces rows 7-8 behind me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6: stepping L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex has survived five rows, but her claimed knowledge is now expendable. I should stay silent and preserve my position while the front absorbs the remaining risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is at the front, has been correct four times. Row 6 is next. I'm second in line, so if Bex fails I step up automatically onto the safe pane. No decision for me this round. I'll stay quiet and let Bex take the risk.

events.name: Eli
